items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: I met Lizzy on a radio interview... I happened to be up there one day and here comes Lizzy Miles... And Lizzy set him straight and we got to talking over there.

ctx.x: Yeah, he plays up there on the 600 blocks.

And he's just, uh, great. Yes, great. But that seems to be the thing now I see with, uh, for popularity. So we're getting back to, it's not folk music and it's not completely blues, but it is a, I believe it's sort of a combination of folk, rhythm, and blues. The style that's evolving now, or gelling, you know, which would be popular for a while. And I hate to think what the next one will be, I don't know. But Lizzy was here, Lizzy Miles, she, um, I met Lizzy on a radio interview. Tony Almericka used to have a…
What about the El Moraco? That was the place where they used to have some, um, George used to play there.

items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: we had Lizzie Miles whom we resurrected... she would do, along with Joe Robichaud, she would do the low... I'd let Liz go away and she'd take some engagements... and she'd come right back to us.

ctx.x: And what have you been playing most nights a week?

Six nights a week. Six nights a week. When he came in as a steady band, you see. And opposed to George, we had Lizzie Miles whom we resurrected. And Lizzie would do, along with Joe Robichaud, she would do the low, you know, the 15 minutes. And of course we went through many, many wonderful people like Kid Howard. We put a band together for Kid Howard and Kid was here for a while. About that time his chops came out and he had to take a respite from it. We were probably using it.
